text: Global temperatures have risen by 1.1 degrees Celsius since pre-industrial times, according to the latest IPCC report. Scientists warn that without immediate action, we could surpass the 1.5-degree threshold within the next decade.

The renewable energy sector saw record investment in 2025, with solar and wind capacity additions outpacing fossil fuels for the third consecutive year. However, grid infrastructure remains a bottleneck.

Critics argue that aggressive climate policies threaten economic growth and energy security. The transition away from fossil fuels must balance environmental goals with affordable energy for consumers.
Community-led climate adaptation projects have shown promising results in developing countries, demonstrating that local solutions can complement international policy frameworks.
The carbon tax debate continues to divide policymakers, with proponents citing its efficiency and opponents warning of regressive impacts on lower-income households.
